title: Safety Violations
titleLabel: Firefighters are entering high-risk, non-compliant factories more often

title: Pingtung: Ming Yang International
stored excess chemicals, sparking a fire
pingtung.body: At 5:31 p.m., a gas explosion at a Ming Yang International warehouse set off a major fire. The company had illegally stored the chemical crosslinking agent C40-P at 30 times the permitted safety limit, and the room temperature exceeded the safe storage temperature. Four firefighters who went in to rescue trapped workers were thrown by the blast wave, burned and struck by flying debris, and died after being taken to hospital.

alt.video: Aerial video of the Ming Yang International warehouse fire
alt.report: Ming Yang International fire investigation report: firefighters killed by the fire triggered by the explosion
alt.photo: Scene of the Ming Yang International warehouse fire

title: Taoyuan: Chin-Poon Industrial breached fire compartments,
letting the fire spread with ease
taoyuan.body: At 9:28 p.m., flames erupted at the Chin-Poon factory. The company had illegally run exhaust ducts through the walls, breaching the fire compartments without authorization, and firefighters only discovered unidentified solvents stored on site after they arrived. Because the building data they held did not match the actual conditions, the firefighters became trapped and could not get out in time. Six died.

alt.video: Video of the Chin-Poon factory fire
alt.report: Comprehensive review report: illegal construction and breached fire compartments let the fire spread
alt.ducts: Exhaust ducts piercing the fire compartment wall to the outside
alt.photo: Scene of the Chin-Poon factory fire

lead: According to the National Fire Agency's 2025 yearbook, fires in factories and warehouses, the categories most prone to industrial safety incidents, nearly doubled over the past decade compared with the decade before. More fires of this kind mean firefighters enter high-risk environments more often, and this is the main reason factory-fire deaths have risen in the past ten years. Central and local government audits of high-risk factories have yet to show clear results, and regulations and inspections need to be enforced more rigorously.

quotes: Dr. Chang Hsien-ho stresses that factories should build their own safety management systems. The simplest way to tell whether a factory is an accident waiting to happen is to look at its office environment and overall management. Factories that end up in disasters are mostly cluttered and chaotic, cutting corners on safety details and neglecting occupational safety rules until catastrophe strikes.

Cheng Shao-shu, deputy chair of the firefighters' rights association, says that after the deadly Xinwu fire in 2015 and the Chin-Poon fire in 2018, Taoyuan now has more complete digital building data for its factories than other cities and counties. Even so, the data firefighters hold is only partial, and conditions on the scene remain full of uncertainty.
